mainTopic: Forbidden images (human face, heavenly bodies), רבן גמליאל's moon diagrams, respectable vs. disgraceful vessels, and how to destroy an idol
overview: The גמרא works out which images a person may not make, based on the פסוקים 'לא תעשון אתי' and 'אשר בשמים'. The human face is forbidden through the reading 'לא תעשון אותי'. אביי tries to limit the ban to the beings of the highest heaven, but a ברייתא forbids making even the sun, moon and stars. The גמרא then defends רבן גמליאל's moon diagrams in several ways: others made them, he was the נשיא and always among the public, they were in pieces, or they were made in order to learn and teach. Along the way it explains the concern of חשדא with raised and sunken ring seals, and why a public place like the shul in נהרדעא is different. It then defines the 'respectable' and 'disgraceful' vessels of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, with רב and שמואל disagreeing and a ברייתא supporting שמואל. Finally, a new משנה brings רבי יוסי's way of destroying an idol and the objection of the חכמים, and the גמרא begins רבי יוסי's answer from a פסוק, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Only the full four-faced figure is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The statement just before this ends here: the תורה only forbade a figure that has all four faces together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה only forbade making a figure with the four faces together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a statement that began just before this: the only figure the תורה forbade is one showing all four faces together. This statement sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heavenly creatures in the vision of יחזקאל each have four faces: human, lion, ox and eagle. This view says the איסור applies only when all four appear together on one figure. A figure showing only one face would then seem to be מותר.

keyTerms.meaning: Four faces, the faces of the heavenly creatures in יחזקאל's vision

phrases.english: The Torah did not forbid
except a figure of the four faces
phrases.notes: These are the four faces of the creatures in יחזקאל 1:10: human, lion, ox and eagle.

phrases.english: together with one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא בִּדְמוּת אַרְבָּעָה פָּנִים בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a statement that began just before this section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The איסור of making figures applies only to a figure with all four faces together.

steps.title: Why is a human face alone forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: If only the full four-faced figure is forbidden, a human face alone should be מותר. Yet a ברייתא forbids the human face.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a human face by itself should be permitted. So why does a ברייתא teach: all faces are permitted except the human face?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the four-faces rule from a ברייתא that singles out the human face as forbidden even when it appears alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the four-faces rule, any single face, including a human one, should be permitted. The ברייתא says every face is permitted except the human face. So the human face alone must be forbidden for some reason the four-faces rule does not explain.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, from now on (introduces a problem that follows from what was just said)
Why then was it taught in a ברייתא?

phrases.english: But if so,
a human face by itself should be permitted!
Why then was it taught in a baraita:
All faces are permitted,
except for the human face?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, פַּרְצוּף אָדָם לְחוֹדֵיהּ תִּשְׁתְּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a consequence from step 1 and shows that a ברייתא contradicts it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that only the four faces together are forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That rule implies a lone human face is permitted, but the ברייתא forbids it.

steps.title: The human face has its own source: 'Do not make Me'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בריה דרב יהושע quotes רבי יהושע: 'לא תעשון אתי' is read as 'לא תעשון אותי', which forbids the human face. Other attendants are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה, son of רב יהושע, said: I heard in a lecture of רבי יהושע: 'You shall not make with Me' means 'You shall not make Me'. But other attendants are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by giving the human face a separate source in the פסוק, apart from the four-faces rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אִתִּי ('with Me') is read as אוֹתִי ('Me'). This creates a separate איסור for the human face, which is the image most closely linked to God. Because the human face has its own source, the ברייתא fits, and other heavenly attendants stay permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Attendants, the heavenly beings who serve God

steps.whyThisMatters: This דרשה is the basis for treating a human face as a forbidden image even on its own.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
I heard it in a lecture of Rabbi Yehoshua:
"You shall not make with Me"
means: you shall not make Me,
phrases.notes: Same letters, read differently: אִתִּי ('with Me') becomes אוֹתִי ('Me').

phrases.english: but other attendants are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: מִפִּרְקֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ שְׁמִיעַ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 2 by giving the human face its own source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The human face would be permitted, since only all four faces together are forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The human face is forbidden because of 'לא תעשון אותי'. Other attendants remain permitted.

steps.title: But a ברייתא forbids figures of the heavenly attendants
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that other attendants are permitted. A ברייתא reads the same פסוק as forbidding figures of אופנים, שרפים, חיות הקודש and מלאכי השרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are other attendants really permitted? But a ברייתא teaches: 'You shall not make with Me' means you shall not make figures of My attendants who serve before Me on high, such as אופנים, שרפים, חיות הקודש and מלאכי השרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last part of רב יהודה's answer, which said that other attendants are permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads 'אתי' as 'those who are with Me', meaning the heavenly attendants. So making figures of them is forbidden. This directly contradicts 'שאר שמשין שרי'.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really permitted? (a challenging question)
אופנים and שרפים, kinds of heavenly beings
The holy creatures of the מרכבה

phrases.english: And are other attendants permitted?
But wasn't it taught in a baraita:
"You shall not make with Me"
means: you shall not make the likeness of My attendants
who serve before Me on high,
such as ofanim and seraphim
and the holy chayyot and the ministering angels!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁאָר שַׁמָּשִׁין מִי שְׁרֵי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the final clause of step 3 ('שאר שמשין שרי').
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that other attendants are permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא reads the same פסוק as forbidding figures of all the heavenly attendants.
steps.whatToRemember: Two readings of 'לא תעשון אתי' are now in play: 'Me', which covers the human face, and 'My attendants', which covers the heavenly beings. The next step explains how they fit together.

steps.title: Only the attendants in the highest heaven are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers the ברייתא from step 4. Only figures of the attendants in the upper heaven, like the angels it listed, are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The תורה only forbade making figures of the attendants that are in the upper level of heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge from step 4. He agrees that angels are forbidden, but limits the ban to the attendants of the highest heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in step 4 forbade figures of אופנים, שרפים, חיות הקודש and מלאכי השרת. אביי accepts this, but he draws a line: only the beings of the top level are included. This suggests that things in the lower heavens, like the sun and moon, may be made.

keyTerms.meaning: Attendants, the beings that serve before הקב״ה
The upper level, meaning the highest heaven

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The Torah did not forbid
anything except the attendants that are in the upper level.
phrases.notes: The top heaven, where the highest angels are. The sun, moon and stars sit in a lower level of heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא שַׁמָּשִׁין שֶׁבַּמָּדוֹר הָעֶלְיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4 by limiting which attendants are forbidden.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule to the highest level
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Step 3 said all other attendants are permitted, so the ברייתא listing angels seemed to contradict it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the attendants of the upper heaven are forbidden. The lower ones are permitted.

steps.title: A ברייתא includes the sun, moon and stars
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי. A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that the sun, moon, stars and constellations are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really permitted to make figures of what is in the lower level? But a ברייתא teaches: 'that is in heaven' includes the sun, moon, stars and constellations, and 'above' includes the ministering angels!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's limit. A ברייתא seems to forbid even the sun, moon and stars, which are in the lower heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי implied that lower heavenly bodies may be made. But the ברייתא reads 'אשר בשמים' as including the sun, moon, stars and constellations. If that ברייתא is about making images, אביי's line falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it permitted? Here it is a challenging question
To include, meaning the word adds something more to the rule

phrases.english: And those in the lower level, are they permitted?
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
"That is in heaven":
to include the sun and the moon,
the stars and the constellations;
"above": to include the ministering angels!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁבְּמָדוֹר הַתַּחְתּוֹן מִי שְׁרֵי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's limit from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that only the attendants of the upper heaven are forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא includes the sun, moon, stars and constellations, which are in the lower heaven. So the lower heaven seems forbidden too.

steps.title: That ברייתא is about worshipping them
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that includes the sun and moon is about worshipping them, not about making their image.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was about worshipping them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי. It says the ברייתא is talking about a different prohibition: worshipping these things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate rules are in play: making an image, and worshipping something. The ברייתא's list is about the ban on worship. So it says nothing against making a picture of the sun or moon, and אביי still stands.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rules. Making a figure of the sun is not the issue in this ברייתא. Worshipping the sun is. Worship is always forbidden.

phrases.english: When that baraita was taught,
it was about worshipping them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תַּנְיָא הָהִיא, לְעוֹבְדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6 by moving the ברייתא to a different prohibition.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the source as being about a different rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was about making images of heavenly bodies.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about worshipping them, so making their images is still permitted.

steps.title: For worship, even a tiny worm should be listed
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא is about worship, why stop at heavenly bodies? Worshipping even a tiny worm is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is about worshipping them, then even a tiny worm is also forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer in step 7. If the topic is worship, the list should not be limited to heavenly things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Worshipping anything at all is forbidden, even the smallest creature. So a ברייתא about worship that names only the sun, moon and stars looks incomplete. This casts doubt on reading it as being about worship.

phrases.english: If it is about worshipping them,
then even a tiny worm is forbidden too!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לְעוֹבְדָם, אֲפִילּוּ שִׁילְשׁוּל קָטָן נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא is about worship
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Worship of even a tiny worm is forbidden, so a worship list should not stop at heavenly bodies.

steps.title: The tiny worm comes from the end of the same פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that a tiny worm is forbidden to worship. That is learned from the end of the same פסוק, as another ברייתא teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true, and it is learned from the end of the פסוק. A ברייתא teaches: 'that is in the earth' includes seas, rivers, mountains and hills, and 'beneath' includes a tiny worm.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees that worshipping a tiny worm is forbidden. It shows that this is learned from a later part of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא only explained the 'heaven' part of the פסוק. The 'earth' part of the פסוק covers earthly things, all the way down to a tiny worm. So nothing is missing, and the reading of step 7, that the ברייתא is about worship, holds.

keyTerms.meaning: From the end of the פסוק
It is learned, it comes out of

steps.whatToRemember: Worship is forbidden for everything: the sun and stars, the seas and mountains, even a tiny worm. Each one is learned from a different part of the same פסוק. אביי's limit on making figures, which covers only the highest heaven, is challenged in the next step.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a clear split between the narrower ban on making images and the total ban on worship. That split shapes how the rest of this topic is understood.

phrases.english: Yes, that is indeed so,
and it is learned from the end of the verse,
as it is taught in a baraita: "That is in the earth":
phrases.notes: Same פסוק as before, שמות 20:4, just its next words.

phrases.english: to include seas and rivers, mountains and hills;
"beneath": to include a tiny worm.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי, וּמִסֵּיפֵיהּ דִּקְרָא נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8 by showing where the worm is learned.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agreeing with the point and showing a different source for it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worship ברייתא leaves out small earthly creatures, so it must not be about worship.
steps.terutzMaskana: Earthly things down to a tiny worm are learned from the end of the פסוק. So the first ברייתא is about worship, and אביי's rule stands.

steps.title: Simply making images of the heavenly bodies is also forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 7. A ברייתא says that just making images of the sun, moon, stars and constellations is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is just making them allowed? But a ברייתא teaches: "You shall not make with Me" means you may not make a likeness of My attendants who serve before Me on high, such as the sun, moon, stars and constellations.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 7 said the ברייתא about the sun and moon was only about worshipping them. Now the גמרא brings a ברייתא that clearly forbids just making their image.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא uses the words 'you shall not make,' so the ban is on making, not only on worship. That means step 7's answer does not work. The question about רבן גמליאל's moon diagrams comes back again.

keyTerms.meaning: Just making it, without worshipping it
My attendants (the heavenly bodies that 'serve' ה׳)

phrases.english: And is just making them permitted?
phrases.notes: He means making an image of the sun or moon without worshipping it.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: "You shall not make with Me"
you shall not make a likeness of My attendants
who serve before Me on high,
such as the sun and moon, the stars and constellations.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַעֲשִׂיָּיה גְּרֵידְתָּא מִי שְׁרֵי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to step 7's answer (that the ברייתא is about worship) and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim (step 5), defended in step 7, that making figures of the lower heavenly bodies such as the sun and moon is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא explicitly forbids making images of the sun, moon and stars, so making them alone is already forbidden.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's diagrams were made by others
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל's case is different, because non-Jews made the diagrams for him. The ban is only on a Jew making them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל is different, because others made them for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new way to defend רבן גמליאל. He did not make the images himself, because non-Jews made them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא accepts that making such images is forbidden. But it says the איסור is on the act of making, not on owning them. Since רבן גמליאל only owned them, he did nothing wrong.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel is different,
because others made them for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, דַּאֲחֵרִים עָשׂוּ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts step 10's ruling and answers the question about רבן גמליאל in a new way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the איסור is on making, and רבן גמליאל did not make them himself.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since making images of the moon is forbidden, רבן גמליאל should not have had them.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only making them is forbidden. Owning images that non-Jews made is allowed.

steps.title: רב יהודה's ring was made by others, yet שמואל had it ruined
steps.stepSummary: Non-Jews made רב יהודה's ring with a human face on it. Still, שמואל told him to ruin the eyes of the image. This suggests that even owning such an image is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at רב יהודה, for whom others made it, and שמואל said to רב יהודה: Sharp one, blind the eyes of this one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 11 with a story. Even when others made the image, שמואל did not allow רב יהודה to keep it whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said that owning an image someone else made is fine. Yet שמואל made רב יהודה ruin an image that others had made. So it seems that owning is also a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Sharp-minded one (a nickname שמואל used for רב יהודה)
Blind its eyes, meaning spoil the image

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַב יְהוּדָה, דַּאֲחֵרִים עָשׂוּ לוֹ,
phrases.english: But there is Rav Yehuda, for whom others made it,
phrases.notes: This was a signet ring with a picture of a person on it.

phrases.english: and Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda:
Sharp one, blind the eyes of this one!
phrases.notes: He means: damage the eyes of the figure so it is no longer a complete image.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַב יְהוּדָה, דַּאֲחֵרִים עָשׂוּ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 11's idea that owning an image others made is allowed.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 11's answer that only making an image is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In רב יהודה's case, others made the image, and שמואל still required it to be ruined. So owning it must also be forbidden.

steps.title: רב יהודה's seal was raised, which looks suspicious
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה's ring had a raised image. שמואל was worried people might suspect it was used for idol worship. That is a different reason from the ban on making images.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it was a raised seal, and the problem was suspicion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. שמואל's ruling was not about owning an image. It was about how it looks to wear a ring with a raised figure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wearing a ring with a raised figure could make people think the owner serves idols. That is the problem of חשדא, which is a separate reason. So step 11's rule still stands: owning an image that others made is fine in itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Suspicion, meaning concern about what people will think

phrases.english: There, it was with a raised seal,
and it was because of suspicion,
phrases.notes: People seeing it might think he owned an idol-worship object.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם בְּחוֹתָמוֹ בּוֹלֵט, וּמִשּׁוּם חֲשָׁדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 and protects step 11's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reason: שמואל's ruling was because of suspicion, not because owning images is forbidden.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's ruling shows that owning an image made by others is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל was concerned about suspicion from a raised image that is worn. Owning an image is not forbidden in itself.

steps.title: A ברייתא about raised and sunken ring seals
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the answer. A ring with a raised seal may not be worn, but it may be used for sealing. A ring with a sunken seal may be worn, but it may not be used for sealing.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: A ring whose seal is raised may not be worn, but one may seal with it. If its seal is sunken, one may wear it, but one may not seal with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that a raised seal on a ring is a problem of suspicion when it is worn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wearing a raised image looks like idol worship, so it is forbidden. Sealing with it is fine, because it leaves only a sunken mark. A sunken seal is fine to wear, but sealing with it creates a raised image, which counts as making a forbidden image.

keyTerms.meaning: To stamp a seal (into wax or clay)

steps.whatToRemember: Making images of the heavenly bodies is forbidden, but owning ones that non-Jews made is allowed. A separate concern is חשדא: wearing a raised image may look like idol worship. A sunken seal is fine to wear, but stamping with it creates a raised image, so it may not be used for sealing.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rules. Wearing is a question of how it looks (חשדא). Sealing is a question of making an image (עשייה). That is why the raised and sunken seals come out opposite.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
A ring whose seal is raised:
it is forbidden to wear it, but permitted to seal with it.
If its seal is sunken, it is permitted to wear it,
but forbidden to seal with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: טַבַּעַת שֶׁחוֹתָמָהּ בּוֹלֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to back up step 13's suspicion answer.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a raised seal on a ring is forbidden to wear because of suspicion, not because owning an image is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about rings with raised and sunken seals.

steps.title: Do we really worry about suspicion? The shul in נהרדעא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea from step 13 that we worry about חשדא. A statue stood in the shul of נהרדעא, yet אבוה דשמואל and לוי prayed there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really worry about people suspecting idol worship? There was a shul in נהרדעא that had been moved there and rebuilt, and a statue was set up inside it. Still, שמואל's father and לוי used to go in and pray there, and they did not worry about suspicion!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave about רב יהודה's ring. If suspicion is a real worry, how could great rabbis pray in a shul that had a statue in it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said שמואל ruined the ring's image because of חשדא. Here we see that אבוה דשמואל and לוי ignored the same kind of suspicion when they prayed near a statue. So it looks like suspicion is not a concern at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Suspicion: the worry that people will think someone worships idols
נהרדעא, a major Jewish town in בבל

phrases.english: And do we worry about suspicion?
But what about the synagogue
that was moved and rebuilt in נהרדעא,
where they set up a statue in it,
phrases.notes: Both words mean 'they set up'. Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and they would go into it,
שמואל's father and לוי,
and they would pray inside it,
and they did not worry about suspicion!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי חָיְישִׁינַן לַחֲשָׁדָא? וְהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason (חשדא) given in step 13 and backed up in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמואל was worried about חשדא with רב יהודה's raised image.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Great rabbis prayed next to a statue without worrying about suspicion, so suspicion should not be a concern.

steps.title: A public place is different
steps.stepSummary: Suspicion does not apply to a public place like a shul. Nobody would think the whole community is worshipping idols there.
steps.simpleTranslation: A public place is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the shul case is different because it belonged to the public. We only worry about suspicion when one private person owns the image.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People do not suspect a whole community of idol worship. They assume the statue is only there for decoration. A private person, like רב יהודה with his ring, can be suspected, so חשדא still applies to him.

phrases.english: The public is different.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּים שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Suspicion seemed not to matter at all, because rabbis prayed near a statue.
steps.terutzMaskana: Suspicion matters for a private person, but not for something that belongs to the public.

steps.title: But רבן גמליאל was one private person
steps.stepSummary: If suspicion matters for a private person, רבן גמליאל was a private person. His moon diagrams should have been a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבן גמליאל was a single person, wasn't he?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the new rule from step 16 against the case of רבן גמליאל. He was one person, so why didn't his moon diagrams cause suspicion?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 explained that רבן גמליאל did not make the diagrams himself. But now we know that owning an image can cause suspicion for a private person. So his diagrams should still have been forbidden because of חשדא.

phrases.english: But wasn't רבן גמליאל a single person?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל דְּיָחִיד הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 16 to raise a new problem with רבן גמליאל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The permission for רבן גמליאל's moon diagrams.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A private person is open to suspicion, and רבן גמליאל was a private person, so his diagrams should have been forbidden.

steps.title: As נשיא, the public was always with him
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל was the נשיא, so the public was always around him. His home counted like a public place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he was the נשיא, many people were always found with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבן גמליאל was not really like a private person. As נשיא, crowds of people were always with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of 'the public is different' from step 16 applies to him too. With so many people around, nobody would suspect idol worship.

keyTerms.meaning: The head of the סנהדרין and leader of the Jewish people

phrases.english: Since he is the נשיא,
many people are found with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּנָשִׂיא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Putting the case into the 'public' category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן גמליאל seemed like a private person who could be suspected.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because he was נשיא, he counts like the public, so there is no suspicion.

steps.title: The diagrams were in pieces
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: רבן גמליאל's diagrams were in separate pieces, not whole images.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: they were in pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer for רבן גמליאל. His diagrams were made of parts that had to be put together, so they were not complete images.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a complete image is a problem. A picture in separate pieces is not forbidden, so there is no issue of making the image and no issue of suspicion.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: introduces another answer

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
they were in pieces.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דִּפְרָקִים הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent answer to step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the object (not a complete image)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The diagrams were full images that a private person owned.
steps.terutzMaskana: Images made of pieces are not forbidden.

steps.title: Making images in order to learn is allowed
steps.stepSummary: A third answer: making images in order to learn is different. A ברייתא on the פסוק 'לא תלמד לעשות' says you may learn in order to understand and to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: making them in order to learn is different. As a ברייתא teaches: 'Do not learn to do' like the disgusting ways of those nations. But you may learn in order to understand and to teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer. רבן גמליאל used the diagrams to learn and to teach how to identify the new moon, and that is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the פסוק carefully. The תורה only forbids learning in order to 'do' the practices of the nations. Learning in order to understand and to give rulings is allowed, so an image made for תורה learning is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do not learn to do': the פסוק in דברים
To understand and to teach or give rulings

steps.whatToRemember: Three reasons explain why רבן גמליאל's moon diagrams were allowed: (1) as נשיא, the public was always with him; (2) the diagrams were in pieces; (3) images made for learning and teaching are permitted.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
for learning, it is different,
as it is taught: 'You shall not learn to do',
but you may learn
in order to understand and to teach.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: ראיה (the ברייתא is support for the answer)
steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, לְהִתְלַמֵּד שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third answer for רבן גמליאל, based on a ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any image of the moon is forbidden to make or to keep.
steps.terutzMaskana: Images made for learning and teaching are permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general rule: some things that are normally forbidden are allowed when they are done to learn and to teach Torah.

steps.title: What counts as respectable or disgraceful vessels?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbids images on respectable vessels and allows them on disgraceful ones. It asks which vessels are which.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, and so on. Which vessels are respectable, and which are disgraceful?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the משנה. It asks for a definition, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said that images on respectable vessels are forbidden and images on disgraceful vessels are allowed. The terms are not clear, so the גמרא asks for a definition of each kind.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on: the rest of the משנה is assumed

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, and so on.
phrases.notes: This is quoting the משנה: images on respectable vessels are forbidden, and images on disgraceful ones are allowed.

phrases.english: Which ones are respectable,
and which ones are disgraceful?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיזוֹ הֵן מְכוּבָּדִין, וְאֵיזוֹ הֵן מְבוּזִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבן גמליאל discussion and returns to the משנה to define its terms.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A definition of 'respectable' and 'disgraceful' vessels in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view.

steps.title: רב: it depends on where the image sits
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that 'respectable' means the image is above the water level on the vessel, and 'disgraceful' means it is below the water level.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: 'Respectable' means the image is above the water. 'Disgraceful' means it is below the water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to the question from Step 21. רב says the difference is not about which kind of vessel it is. It is about where on the vessel the image is placed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב's view, the same pot could carry a respectable image or a disgraceful one. An image high up, above what is inside, is treated with honor. An image down in the water or food is treated with disrespect, so no one would think it is being honored.

keyTerms.meaning: respectable, honored (images people treat with respect)

phrases.english: Rav says:
Respectable — above the water,
phrases.notes: He means where the image sits on the vessel: higher than the water or food inside it.

phrases.english: Disgraceful — below the water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מְכוּבָּדִין — לְמַעְלָה מִן הַמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which images are respectable and which are disgraceful
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It depends on where the image sits relative to the water inside the vessel

steps.title: שמואל: it depends on the type of item
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says any image on a cooking or eating vessel is disgraceful. Respectable images are those on jewelry: bracelets, nose rings and rings.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל says: Both of those places are disgraceful. Rather, respectable images are the ones on bracelets, nose rings and rings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer. שמואל disagrees with רב and says that every spot on a vessel used for food is disgraceful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב drew the line at the water level. שמואל draws the line by the kind of object. Jewelry is worn proudly, so an image on it is honored. A pot is used for everyday work, so any image on it is treated with disrespect.

phrases.english: And Shmuel says:
These and those are disgraceful,
rather, these are respectable:
those on bracelets
and on nose rings and on rings.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ מְבוּזִּין הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing answer to רב's answer in Step 22
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which images are respectable and which are disgraceful
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Images on jewelry are respectable; images on any food vessel are disgraceful

steps.title: A ברייתא supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists jewelry as respectable, and pots, kettles, water heaters, sheets and towels as disgraceful. This matches שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches like שמואל: Respectable images are on bracelets, nose rings and rings. Disgraceful images are on pots, kettles, water heaters, sheets and towels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא calls whole cooking vessels disgraceful and does not split them by the water line, which is what רב did. It also adds cloth items like sheets and towels to the disgraceful list. This shows the line is drawn by the type of object, as שמואל said.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא teaches in agreement with him

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on what 'respectable' means. רב goes by where the image sits relative to the water. שמואל goes by the type of item: jewelry is respectable, and pots and cloths are disgraceful. The ברייתא supports שמואל.

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא in agreement with Shmuel:
Respectable — those on bracelets,
and on nose rings, and on rings;
Disgraceful — those on large pots,
and on kettles, and on water heaters,
and those on sheets, and on towels.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's view from Step 23
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that the category depends on the type of item
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing jewelry as respectable and cooking vessels and cloths as disgraceful

steps.title: רבי יוסי: grind the idol and scatter it
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. רבי יוסי says an idol should be ground up, and the dust scattered in the wind or thrown into the sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי יוסי says: He grinds it up and scatters it to the wind, or throws it into the sea.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי יוסי teaches how to get rid of an idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's goal is to destroy the idol completely and send it far away, so that no one can use it. This sets up the objection of the חכמים in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: the משנה (a new section of the משנה begins here)

phrases.english: Mishnah: Rabbi Yosei says:
He grinds it and scatters it to the wind,
phrases.notes: 'He' is a person who has an idol and needs to destroy it.

phrases.english: or throws it into the sea.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: שׁוֹחֵק וְזוֹרֶה לָרוּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, after the discussion of images ended
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An idol is destroyed by grinding it and scattering the dust in the wind or throwing it into the sea

steps.title: The Rabbis object: the dust becomes fertilizer
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say that scattered dust becomes fertilizer, which gives a person benefit. The פסוק forbids any benefit from something banned.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: That too becomes fertilizer, as it says: 'Nothing of the banned thing shall stick to your hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים challenge רבי יוסי's method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dust scattered on the wind lands on fields and helps crops grow. That is a kind of benefit from an idol, and the פסוק forbids even the smallest amount of benefit from something banned.

keyTerms.meaning: something banned and forbidden for any benefit

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: 'They' are the חכמים who disagree with רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: That too becomes fertilizer,
as it is said:
"Nothing of the banned thing shall stick to your hand."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אַף הוּא נַעֲשֶׂה זֶבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוסי's ruling in Step 25
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's method of scattering the dust or throwing it into the sea
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The scattered dust becomes fertilizer, which is a benefit, and the פסוק forbids any benefit from something banned

steps.title: רבי יוסי begins answering with a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a ברייתא in which רבי יוסי answers the חכמים by quoting a פסוק that begins 'And your sin.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It is taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי said to them: But has it not already been said: 'And your sin...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a ברייתא in which רבי יוסי defends his view with a פסוק. The פסוק continues in the next part, so this step is setting up his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי does not accept the objection of the חכמים. He brings a פסוק to show that destroying something forbidden by grinding and scattering it is a proper way to do it. We will see the full proof when the quote continues.

keyTerms.meaning: but has it not already been said (introduces a proof from a פסוק)

phrases.english: Gemara: It is taught in a ברייתא,
Rabbi Yosei said to them,
But has it not already been said:
"And your sin
phrases.notes: דברים 9:21. The פסוק keeps going in the next part of the גמרא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוסי answers the challenge of the חכמים from Step 26
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי's method of grinding the idol and scattering the dust
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק beginning 'ואת חטאתכם', which continues in the next part
